metas.name: Annihilation
metas.description:
Everything that passes through the Shimmer comes out refracted. A team enters it, where light, radio, DNA and memory are mixed across channels like a signal through a prism — plants shaped like people, animals carrying other species' traits.

A biologist signs up for a dangerous, secret expedition in which the laws of nature don't apply.

metas.name: Possession
metas.description:
A marriage breaks down as literal hysteria. A couple in Berlin tearing each other apart, in Isabelle Adjani's unhinged performance — domestic, then completely not.

A woman starts exhibiting increasingly disturbing behavior after asking her husband for a divorce. Suspicions of infidelity soon give way to something much more sinister.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description:
Fame eats away at a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

A pop singer gives up her career to become an actress, but she slowly goes insane when she starts being stalked by an obsessed fan and what seems to be a ghost of her past.

metas.name: Cure
metas.description:
Emptiness spreads from person to person. A Tokyo detective investigates murders where each killer is different, calm, and cannot explain themselves — hypnotic and grey rather than jumpy.

A frustrated detective deals with the case of several gruesome murders committed by people who have no recollection of what they've done.

metas.name: The Witch
metas.description:
Religious paranoia eats a family from inside its own beliefs. Puritan settlers exiled to a forest's edge: a crop fails, a baby vanishes, and their theology gives them only one interpretation.

An isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England comes unraveled by the forces of witchcraft and possession.

metas.name: Lake Mungo
metas.description:
Grief takes the form of a family documentary. Found footage, but the subject is not the ghost — it is parents and a brother in interviews, months after a drowning, still looking for anything.

Strange things start happening after a girl is found drowned in a lake.

metas.name: Safe
metas.description:
A suburban life turns out so empty that a woman becomes allergic to modernity itself. In perfect pastel houses, symptoms no doctor can find, and a drift toward a desert self-help commune.

An affluent and unexceptional homemaker in the suburbs develops multiple chemical sensitivity.

metas.name: Hereditary
metas.description:
In this family, grief and resentment were already there before anything supernatural arrived. A grandmother dies, a mother builds miniature scenes of her life, and a dinner-table argument is the scariest sequence.

A grieving family is haunted by tragic and disturbing occurrences.

metas.name: Leviathan
metas.description:
Commercial fishing becomes a sensory ordeal. Cameras strapped to nets, chains, helmets and the hull of a North Atlantic trawler — fish heads, gulls, diesel, men half-asleep at 3 a.m., no explanation offered.

A documentary shot in the North Atlantic and focused on the commercial fishing industry.

metas.name: Under the Skin
metas.description:
Human beings, seen from outside the species, look like this. A woman drives a van around Glasgow picking up men, in real streets with hidden cameras and non-actors, and something in the routine begins to fail — images that lodge permanently.

A mysterious young woman seduces lonely men in the evening hours in Scotland. However, events lead her to begin a process of self-discovery.

metas.name: Funny Games
metas.description:
Your appetite as a viewer is the real subject, and the film refuses to feed it the usual way. Two polite young men hold a family at their holiday house; violence happens off-screen or gets rewound, and the film keeps asking why you're still watching.

Two violent young men take a mother, father, and son hostage in their vacation cabin and force them to play sadistic "games" with one another for their own amusement.

metas.name: Videodrome
metas.description:
A TV signal gets inside a man's body. A sleazy Toronto cable programmer finds a pirate broadcast of torture, becomes obsessed, and his perception and flesh start reorganising around it.

A Toronto cable TV station co-owner who specializes in adult entertainment searches for the producers of a dangerous and bizarre broadcast titled "Videodrome."

metas.name: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
metas.description:
A vampire film gets rebuilt from Iranian, Western and skate-punk parts. A fictional Iranian ghost town, a chador-wearing vampire on a skateboard, a drug dealer and a cat, in long black-and-white silences between bursts of pop.

In the Iranian ghost-town Bad City, a place that reeks of death and loneliness, the townspeople are unaware they are being stalked by a lonesome vampire.

metas.name: Pi
metas.description:
A pattern becomes an obsession, filmed on grain. A mathematician in a tiny New York apartment with computers made of junk, a number that Wall Street and a Hasidic sect both want, and migraines rendered as drill sounds.

A paranoid mathematician searches for a key number that will unlock the universal patterns found in nature.

metas.name: Audition
metas.description:
Loneliness curdles into horror while the film changes genre around it. A widower holds fake auditions to find a wife; the first hour is a sad, gentle drama before the film reveals what it actually was.

A widower has his film producer friend organize a fake audition as a means of helping him find a new girlfriend, but the woman he selects is not who she appears to be.

metas.name: The Lighthouse
metas.description:
Two men rot in each other's company. A rock in a storm, gaslight, seagull taboos, and two keepers descending into myth, flatulence and murder inside a frame almost square enough to be a trap.

Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.

metas.name: The Act of Seeing with One's Own Eyes
metas.description:
The camera is reduced to pure looking: Brakhage films autopsies in a Pittsburgh morgue silently and in close-up, with no commentary to hide behind, asking whether there is anything a camera should refuse to see.

At a morgue, forensic pathologists conduct autopsies of the corpses assigned. "S. Brakhage, entering, WITH HIS CAMERA, one of the forbidden, terrific locations of our culture, the autopsy room. It is a place wherein, inversely, life is cherished, for it exists to affirm that no one of us may die without our knowing exactly why. All of us, in the person of the coroner, must see that, for ourselves, with our own eyes. It is a room full of appalling particular intimacies, the last ditch of individuation. Here our vague nightmare of mortality acquires the names and faces of OTHERS. This last is a process that requires a WITNESS; and what 'idea' may finally have inserted itself into the sensible world we can still scarcely guess, for the CAMERA would seem the perfect Eidetic Witness, staring with perfect compassion where we can scarcely bear to glance." – Hollis Frampton

metas.name: Häxan
metas.description:
A lecture dissolves into delirium in Christensen's silent Swedish study of witchcraft, which keeps abandoning its own format for re-enactments — sabbaths, torture chambers, possessed nuns — and from 1922 remains wilder than most folk horror made since.

Fictionalized documentary showing the evolution of witchcraft, from its pagan roots to its confusion with hysteria in Eastern Europe.

metas.name: The Wicker Man
metas.description:
Paganism appears in this film not as horror but as joy. A devout Christian policeman arrives on a Scottish island where the harvest failed and the old religion quietly resumed — and the islanders keep bursting into song, which is what makes the ending land.

A puritan police sergeant arrives in a Scottish island village in search of a missing girl, who the pagan locals claim never existed.

metas.name: Kwaidan
metas.description:
Kobayashi builds folklore out of pure painted atmosphere. He adapts Lafcadio Hearn's ghost tales on vast studio sets — a snow spirit, a blind biwa player performing for the dead — the closest Japanese equivalent to Parajanov's tableau method.

A collection of four Japanese folk tales with supernatural themes.

metas.name: The Company of Wolves
metas.description:
Jordan and Angela Carter restore the folk tale's actual content — appetite, danger, metamorphosis — that the children's versions politely remove. They nest werewolf tales inside a sleeping girl's dream, all fog, forests and practical-effect transformations.

A teenage girl in a country manor falls asleep while reading a magazine, and has a disturbing dream involving wolves prowling the woods below her bedroom window.

metas.name: Viy
metas.director: Aleksandr Ptushko, Konstantin Ershov, Georgiy Kropachyov
metas.description:
This folk tale is told at full demonic strength. A seminarian must pray three nights over a witch's corpse in a village church; Soviet special effects, a Gogol story, and a final night that still startles.

A young priest is ordered to preside over the wake of witch in a small old wooden church of a remote village. This means spending three nights alone with the corpse with only his faith to protect him.

metas.name: A Page of Madness
metas.description:
Madness is experienced from inside the asylum walls, in 1926, with no intertitles. A janitor works at the institution holding his wife; the editing itself loses its grip — closer to a panic attack than a silent film.

A man takes a job at an asylum with hopes of freeing his imprisoned wife.

metas.name: The Housemaid
metas.description:
A home is invaded by its own employee. A composer hires a maid; she takes the house apart floor by floor — piano lessons, rat poison, a staircase that becomes the film's moral geometry. Korean melodrama at fever pitch, restored from near-loss.

A composer and his wife are thrown into turmoil when a housemaid becomes more than they bargained for.

metas.name: Timecrimes
metas.description:
In this time loop, a man becomes his own haunting. A guy with binoculars, a bandaged stranger, a scientist with a tank — three trips through one hour, each pass reassigning who the villain is. The tightest loop mechanics ever filmed, on a Spanish hillside with almost no budget.

A man accidentally gets into a time machine and travels back in time nearly an hour. Finding himself will be the first of a series of disasters of unforeseeable consequences.

metas.name: One Cut of the Dead
metas.description:
A film set survives its own film. The first half-hour is a wobbly one-take zombie short; then the film rewinds and shows you the production, and every wobble becomes a joke with a fuse on it. Engineered joy — don't read anything else about it.

Things go badly for a hack director and film crew shooting a low budget zombie movie in an abandoned WWII Japanese facility, when they are attacked by real zombies.

metas.name: What We Do in the Shadows
metas.description:
Four vampires fail at flatshare administration. Wellington's undead argue about the dishes roster, dress codes for clubs and a rival werewolf pack ("we're werewolves, not swearwolves") in deadpan documentary form. Deliberately, disarmingly light.

Viago, Deacon, and Vladislav are vampires who are struggling with the mundane aspects of modern life, like paying rent, keeping up with the chore wheel, trying to get into nightclubs, and overcoming flatmate conflicts.

metas.name: Kuroneko
metas.description:
A ghost story is staged like Noh theatre in a bamboo grove. A mother and daughter-in-law, murdered by samurai, return as cat-spirits sworn to drink samurai blood — until one victim is their own son and husband. Mist, wire-work leaps, and vengeance colliding with the vow that powers it.

Two women are raped and killed by samurai soldiers. Soon they reappear as vengeful ghosts who seduce and brutally murder the passing samurai.

metas.name: Wisdom Teeth
metas.description:
A man has a wisdom tooth pulled, and his friend asks to pull the stitches. Five minutes, one dental thread, escalating commitment to a single bad idea.

Nigel does his best to help with his friend's simple request.

metas.name: Humane
metas.description:
A state euthanasia programme plays out inside an Ontario mansion. Facing ecological collapse, the government asks citizens to enlist for euthanasia to cut the population by twenty percent, with a payment to the family; a wealthy patriarch announces at dinner that he and his wife have signed up, and the evening becomes the policy's real content — inheritance, guilt and persuasion administered as a family argument. Polite recruiters included.

In the wake of an environmental collapse that is forcing humanity to shed 20% of its population, a family dinner erupts into chaos when a father's plan to enlist in the government's new euthanasia program goes horribly awry.
